newsitem.title: UK: BA says American deal still on track.
newsitem.headline: BA says American deal still on track.

text.p: British Airways remained optimistic on Tuesday that its proposed alliance with American Airlines would take off this summer despite the threat of a clash with the European Commission (EC).

"The deal...is planned to be implemented during the course of the early summer of this year and I see no reason why it should not be possible to achieve that timetable," British Airways Chief Executive Robert Ayling told BBC radio.

On Monday EC sources said Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert had told Britain the EC would not tolerate British approval of the deal if it conflicted with the Commission's own views. In a letter sent to British Trade Secretary Ian Lang's department, Van Miert said the Commission would defend its view in the European Court of Justice if necessary.
Asked about this apparent EC challenge to British proposals to conditionally approve the deal, Ayling said, "I remain optimistic that we can get through this and get approval."

In December Lang proposed conditions for allowing the alliance to go ahead, including a demand that the companies release a total of 168 weekly runway slots at London Heathrow airport to make room for more competition.
But an EU source said that 168 slots would not be enough to ensure adequate competition -- the Commission would want a figure nearer 300 to 400 and these slots would have to be surrendered, not sold.
